description: City explores central navigation hub to address homelessness.
Study proposes network of hubs for coordinated services.
Potential costs range from $9 million to $32 million.
Partnership with province is essential for implementation.

chips.text: Mayor Block emphasized a central hub is crucial for homeless individuals to access services.
How mini-hubs with civic facilities would alleviate service duplication remains unclear.
Over 80% of homeless individuals identify as Indigenous, needing cultural services.
Administration will provide a roadmap and status updates by Q2 2026.

segments.title: Community Navigation Hub Feasibility Study Overview
description: Homelessness numbers nearly tripled in past two years.
Temporary measures are unsustainable and resource-intensive.
Study proposes a network model with central, mini, and seasonal hubs.
Hubs would provide diverse services and reduce system strain.

chips.text: Capital costs range from $9M to $32M for a central hub
1500 individuals identified last October as lacking permanent shelter
Proposes a navigation hub network model as a new service delivery model

segments.title: Clarifying Hub Terminology and Duplication
description: Councillor Keller asked about "low barrier," "basic," and "enhanced" terms.
Administration clarified "basic" and "low barrier" are similar.
Question raised on how civic mini-hubs avoid service duplication.

chips.text: How would mini hubs alleviate duplication of services?

segments.title: Mayor Block's Questions on Hub Models and Funding
description: Mayor Block inquired about the concept of mini hubs.
Asked about the scope of services in mini hubs.
Questioned how fundraising models would be catalyzed.

segments.title: Federal Funding Allocation for Homelessness Initiatives
description: Councillor Dubois asked about the $4.43 million federal funding.
Feasibility study cost was minimal from this fund.
Remaining funds for 30 supportive housing units and warming/cooling space.
$275,000 contributes to permanent shelter construction.

chips.text: $4.43 million federal funding for homelessness initiatives

segments.title: Councillor Tidemore's Concern on Service Concentration
description: Councillor Tidemore concerned about concentrating services downtown.
Cited resident and business concerns about existing concentration.
Stressed need for engagement to address these concerns.

chips.text: Residents and businesses concerned about service concentration

segments.title: Motion to Advance Central Hub Work
description: Councillor Keller moved a motion to advance feasibility study work.
Administration found initial Q1 2026 timeline challenging.
Friendly amendment changed reporting deadline to Q2 2026.

chips.text: Reporting deadline changed to Q2 2026 for all recommendations
Q1 will be very challenging to provide a further report

segments.title: Debate on Central Hub Focus
description: Councillor McDonald questioned if motion precluded multi-hub options.
Councillor Keller confirmed focus on a central hub.
Mayor Block supported central hub as a "one-stop shop."

chips.text: A central navigation hub is what we need
Homeless people face immense walking to access basic services

segments.title: Administration's Commitment and Clarifications
description: Administration confirmed Q2 2026 is a more realistic reporting deadline.
Committed to driving forward as fast and thoroughly as possible.
Clarified city would not be involved in social service provision.
Confirmed motion focuses on single hub, not precluding future options.

chips.text: We will drive forward as fast and thoroughly as we can
The focus is on the single hub model

segments.title: Engagement and Premature Motion Concerns
description: Councillor McDonald questioned if adequate engagement could be done by Q2.
Administration stated engagement with service providers and government is necessary.
Councillor McDonald felt the motion was premature without more service detail.
Councillor Parker concerned about lack of lived experience input and single hub.

chips.text: Can adequate community engagement be done by Q2 2026?
This is premature without more service detail

segments.title: Final Comments and Motion Carries
description: Chair concerned about city funding provincial jurisdiction.
Expressed concern about single hub decision and aggressive timelines.
Hoped for interim updates if full report not ready by Q2 2026.
Councillor Keller's motions carried unanimously.

chips.text: Councillor Keller's motions carried unanimously
We'll go broke if we keep doing everything the province is supposed to do
